rubric / evaluation-framework.md8 criteria · Select one

The evaluation rubric, opened up

The personal framework behind the project above, combined with criteria used daily on Outlier AI, Scale AI, Appen, OneForma and Test IO work.

Factual accuracy

factual-accuracy.md
  • Every factual claim is verified — independent research and cross-referencing.
  • Factual errors are separated from opinion, inference and uncertain claims.
  • Unsupported claims are called out, even when plausible.
Flagged when: hallucinations, misinformation or unsupported claims appear.

Instruction-following

  • Judged against what was actually asked, not what it chose to answer.
  • Compliance with project guidelines, format, scope and constraints.
Flagged when: requirements are missed or constraints ignored.

Logical consistency

  • Read end-to-end for internal consistency — no contradictions.
  • Logical gaps identified systematically.
Flagged when: inconsistencies, contradictions or reasoning failures are found.

Communication quality

  • Clarity, grammar and written accuracy.
  • Tone appropriate and consistent throughout.
Flagged when: tonal inconsistencies or unclear writing undermine the answer.

Reasoning quality

  • The reasoning itself is judged, not just the final answer.
  • Stronger reasoning wins side-by-side comparisons.
Flagged when: broken chains, skipped steps or unsupported conclusions.

Relevance

  • Relevance to the request, plus depth and usefulness for the audience.
Flagged when: off-topic, padded, or correct but not useful.

Completeness

  • Every part of the request covered — multi-part prompts checked part by part.
Flagged when: parts are left unanswered or the response stops short.

Safety

  • Reviewed as a standing criterion on every response, against project safety guidelines.
Flagged when: content breaches safety guidelines, whatever its other scores.

2024—professional evaluation work

§01 The rubric — eight inspections

A personal framework built from 900+ hours of study, combined with the criteria used daily in professional evaluation work. Every response is scored, compared side-by-side, and justified in writing. Each inspection below names what is checked — and what gets flagged.

01

Factual accuracy

Every factual claim is verified — independent research and cross-referencing. Factual errors are separated from opinion, inference and uncertain claims, and unsupported claims are called out, even when plausible.

Hallucinations, misinformation or unsupported claims
02

Instruction-following

Judged against what was actually asked, not what it chose to answer — compliance with project guidelines, format, scope and constraints.

Requirements missed or constraints ignored
03

Logical consistency

Read end-to-end for internal consistency — no contradictions; logical gaps identified systematically.

Inconsistencies, contradictions or reasoning failures
04

Communication quality

Clarity, grammar and written accuracy, with tone appropriate and consistent throughout.

Tonal inconsistencies or unclear writing
05

Reasoning quality

The reasoning itself is judged, not just the final answer — stronger reasoning wins side-by-side comparisons.

Broken chains, skipped steps or unsupported conclusions
06

Relevance

Relevance to the request, plus depth and usefulness for the audience.

Off-topic, padded, or correct but not useful
07

Completeness

Every part of the request covered — multi-part prompts checked part by part.

Parts left unanswered or the response stops short
08

Safety

Reviewed as a standing criterion on every response, against project safety guidelines.

Any breach of safety guidelines, whatever its other scores

§02 How a verdict is reached

1STEP 01Score against the rubric

Each criterion scored independently against structured guidelines.

2STEP 02Compare & rank

Side-by-side comparison of competing responses under the same criteria.

3STEP 03Justify in writing

Detailed written feedback supporting every decision and ranking.
